record.title: Mortar round wounds Thai soldier; Cambodia calls it operational error
record.detail: Thailand's army said a mortar round fired from the Cambodian side wounded one Thai soldier in Ubon Ratchathani, calling it a breach of the 27 Dec ceasefire; the Thai military said Cambodia described it as an unintentional operational error.
record.attribution: Thai army claims, Cambodian explanation as relayed by Thai military, via Al Jazeera

record.title: National Bank places Prince Bank into liquidation
record.detail: The NBC suspended all new services at Prince Bank and appointed a liquidator two days after Prince Group chairman Chen Zhi was extradited to China; the bank had been sanctioned by the US and UK in Oct 2025.

record.title: Over 10,000 displaced still barred from homes along Thai border
record.detail: Provincial officials said about 9,000 people (2,735 families) in Banteay Meanchey plus families in Pursat, Preah Vihear and Oddar Meanchey could not return home despite the ceasefire; over 173,000 remained in camps. Thailand denies territorial expansion.

record.title: First human H5N1 case of 2026 in Kampot
record.detail: The Ministry of Health confirmed H5N1 in a 30-year-old man from Tuek Chhou district, Kampot, who had cooked dead chickens at home; he recovered and was discharged, and contacts received Tamiflu.

record.title: Hun Manet says Thai forces occupy territory deep inside Cambodia
record.detail: PM Hun Manet claimed Thai troops placed containers and barbed wire in Cambodian areas of Pursat and Banteay Meanchey, keeping about 80,000 people from home; Thailand has previously said it only holds Thai territory.
record.attribution: Hun Manet claims via Al Jazeera

record.title: Night blaze kills four in Russei Keo
record.detail: A fire in Boeung Salang village destroyed three flats, killing four and injuring five; the Phnom Penh fire department deployed 22 water tenders and said the cause was under investigation.

record.title: Thai navy seizes Cambodian fishing boat near Koh Yor; MFA protests
record.detail: Cambodia's foreign ministry said the Thai navy arrested three Cambodians and seized a fishing boat about 7.2 nm from Koh Yor, Koh Kong, calling it a violation of Cambodian territorial sea; Thailand says the boat was in Thai waters.
record.agency: Ministry of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation
record.attribution: Cambodian MFA claims via CamboJA News

record.title: Middle East conflict disrupts Gulf-linked flights to Cambodia
record.detail: The State Secretariat of Civil Aviation said 52 weekly Middle East-linked flights (46 via Techo International, 6 via Siem Reap-Angkor) were affected by airspace closures after strikes on Iran from 28 Feb, with up to 12,960 passengers a week at risk.

record.title: Rain floods border displacement camp in Thmar Pouk
record.detail: Heavy rain flooded the Wat Kandol pagoda camp sheltering about 1,631 displaced families in Thmar Pouk district; about 400 families moved to higher ground, a district deputy governor said.
record.attribution: District officials and residents via CamboJA News

record.title: 77 foreigners detained at Ream online-fraud site
record.detail: Provincial police led by a deputy governor raided the Silong Bay Borey site in Sangkat Ream, detaining 77 foreigners and seizing 77 computers and phones.

record.title: Fourth human H5N1 case of 2026 confirmed in Svay Rieng
record.detail: The Ministry of Health confirmed H5N1 in a 66-year-old woman in Svay Rieng who had contact with infected poultry at home, the fourth human case of 2026; Institut Pasteur researchers have flagged a novel reassortant strain.
record.agency: Ministry of Health / Institut Pasteur du Cambodge

record.title: EDC deploys temporary substations as energy crisis strains grid
record.detail: Électricité du Cambodge deployed two 75 MW temporary modular substations on the 230 kV network at Veal Rinh (Preah Sihanouk) and Samrong Yong (Takeo), and the National Assembly is reviewing a law guaranteeing payments for Vietnamese power imports to 2030.
record.place: Veal Rinh and Samrong Yong substations

record.title: Defence minister welcomes plan for General Border Committee meeting
record.detail: Deputy PM and Defence Minister Tea Seiha welcomed a Thai suggestion for a GBC meeting, the first since 27 Dec 2025; Thailand's defence minister said reopening checkpoints would be the final step. About 32,000 Cambodians remained displaced.
record.attribution: Defence ministers' statements via The Star/ANN

record.title: Two worker-transport crashes kill 14 garment workers
record.detail: A cargo truck hit an open-top worker transport in Kampong Chhnang (9 dead, 53 injured) and a bus carrying workers overturned in Svay Rieng (5 dead, 40 injured); the Labour Ministry urged stricter traffic compliance.
record.agency: Ministry of Labour and Vocational Training

record.title: 64 Chinese nationals arrested at Sihanoukville casino scam site
record.detail: Preah Sihanouk authorities and prosecutors raided the Ying Huang casino in Sangkat 4, arresting 64 Chinese nationals and seizing 428 phones and 37 computers.

record.title: Single lightning strike kills three rice farmers in Pursat
record.detail: Local police said lightning killed three farmers sowing rice in Meteuk commune, Bakan district, on the afternoon of 28 May; the same day lightning killed 19 cattle in Lumphat, Ratanakiri.

record.title: 111 detained, 108 Indonesians, in Sihanoukville scam raid
record.detail: The Sihanoukville unified command and provincial prosecutor detained 111 people in Sangkat 4, including 108 Indonesians (37 women) processed for deportation, and seized 117 laptops and 415 phones.

record.title: OFAC expands Prince Group sanctions; FinCEN widens Huione rule
record.detail: OFAC designated 9 individuals and 26 entities linked to Prince Group, including second-in-command Hu Xiaowei and companies in the UK, BVI, Hong Kong and Singapore; FinCEN proposed extending its Huione Group rule to H-Pay Service PLC and successors.
record.attribution: OFAC/FinCEN actions summarised by HSF Kramer

record.title: CDC: Cambodia had 4 human H5N1 cases and 1 death in H1 2026
record.detail: The US CDC global summary counted four human H5N1 cases in Cambodia from January to June 2026 (onsets in February, March and April), one fatal, all linked to sick or dead backyard poultry and clade 2.3.2.1e viruses.

record.title: Landmine/UXO casualties reach 28 in first half of 2026
record.detail: CMAA said mines and explosive remnants of war caused 28 casualties in H1 2026 (7 killed, 15 injured, 6 amputees), up 16.6% from 24 a year earlier.
record.agency: Cambodian Mine Action and Victim Assistance Authority (CMAA)

record.title: NCDM: lightning killed 16 in H1 2026, down 48% on 2025
record.detail: The National Committee for Disaster Management reported 16 lightning deaths and 18 injuries in the first half of 2026 (31 deaths a year earlier), plus 3 deaths and 9 injuries from other storm impacts.

record.title: Fifth human H5N1 case of 2026: infant in Phnom Penh
record.detail: The Ministry of Health confirmed H5N1 in a nine-month-old girl in Meanchey district, Phnom Penh, who was in intensive care; it was the country's fifth human case of 2026.

record.title: Immigration says 16,000 foreigners deported for scam involvement in H1
record.detail: General Department of Immigration chief Lt Gen Sok Veasna said 16,000 foreigners were deported for involvement in scam compounds in the first half of 2026, out of 45,000 deportations overall; about 2,000 people were refused entry.
record.attribution: Immigration department figures via AGB/Khmer Times

record.title: Battery recycling site fire spews toxic smoke in Kampong Speu
record.detail: A fire and explosions at an unpermitted lithium battery and metal recycling site in Samaki Mony Chey district produced toxic smoke into 30 Jul, killing about 2,000 chickens at a nearby farm; the Ministry of Environment ordered penalties and health officials urged residents to wear masks.
record.place: Tuol Sambour village, Damnak Raing commune
record.attribution: Ministry of Environment findings via The Star/ANN

record.title: EU sanctions Prince Holding Group, Chen Zhi and Jin Bei Group
record.detail: The EU listed Prince Holding Group, its chairman Chen Zhi, Sihanoukville-based Jin Bei Group and its chairman Zhu Zhongbiao under its global human-rights sanctions regime, citing at least 10 forced-labour scam compounds in Cambodia; asset freezes and travel bans apply.

record.title: Road deaths up 11% to 773 in H1 after enforcement pause
record.detail: Interior Minister Sar Sokha told the PM that H1 2026 saw 1,279 crashes, 773 deaths and 1,944 injuries, up from 694 deaths a year earlier, blaming a pause in traffic-law enforcement; he sought to resume strict enforcement from 1 Sep.

record.title: NCDM and water ministry order flood preparedness as rivers rise
record.detail: NCDM issued a directive and the Ministry of Water Resources and Meteorology an advisory on 19 Aug warning of rising Mekong, Bassac and Tonle Sap levels and heavy rain from storm Saudel through 29 Aug, with coastal seas of 0.5-1.75 m.
record.agency: National Committee for Disaster Management; Ministry of Water Resources and Meteorology
record.attribution: NCDM and MOWRAM warnings via Cambodianess

record.title: 35 foreigners detained in Sihanoukville hotel scam raid
record.detail: Provincial gendarmerie under the unified command raided the 22-storey Chun Yi Hotel in Sangkat 3, detaining 35 foreigners including four women and seizing computers and 55 phones linked to fraud.

record.title: Mekong floods affect 13,688 families after Typhoon Saudel
record.detail: NCDM said Mekong flooding that began around 22-23 Aug affected 13,688 families in Kratie, Tboung Khmum, Stung Treng and Kampong Cham, with 1,551 families evacuated, over 9,000 homes inundated and over 4,000 ha of rice submerged; no casualties reported.

record.title: Anti-scam commission claims Cambodia has no remaining scam compounds
record.detail: CCOS, headed by Senior Minister Chhay Sinarith, claimed that from July 2025 to 20 Aug 2026 it investigated 793 suspected sites, raided 624, detained nearly 30,000 people of 39 nationalities and deported 58,266 foreigners; anti-trafficking experts disputed the claim that scam operations were eradicated.

record.title: 19,652 drug suspects held, 2.65 t narcotics seized Jan-Aug
record.detail: Cambodian authorities reported 7,347 drug cases and 19,652 suspects detained in Jan-Aug 2026, with 2.65 t of narcotics, 282 kg of marijuana and 2.26 t of precursor chemicals seized.

record.title: Former Kiribati president says China's missile test sent a 'message'
record.detail: ABC reports a former Kiribati president said China's missile test into the Pacific was meant to send a message; that is the former president's claim.

record.title: Kiribati and Nauru stir frustration over China at the Forum
record.detail: ABC reports Kiribati and Naoero caused frustration at the Pacific Islands Forum over their positions on China.

record.title: Kiribati detains Chinese vessel carrying banned shark fin
record.detail: Kiribati detained a Chinese-flagged fishing vessel found with banned shark fins, the Taipei Times reported (also Daily Tribune, 25 Aug).

record.title: Kiribati weighs constitutional change on China recognition
record.detail: ABC reported Kiribati was considering amending its constitution to cement diplomatic recognition of the People's Republic of China.

record.title: Kiribati snubbed at Pacific Islands Forum closing
record.detail: 1News reports Kiribati was left out at the closing of the Pacific Islands Forum, which was described as disappointing.

record.title: Two ballistic missiles fired from Pyongyang toward East Sea
record.detail: Japan's MoD and South Korea's JCS detected two ballistic missiles launched from Ryokpho district around 07:50, flying roughly 900-950 km. KCNA claimed hypersonic missiles hit targets 1,000 km away (KCNA claim).
record.agency: ROK Joint Chiefs of Staff / Japan Ministry of Defense
record.attribution: JCS, Japan MoD; weapon claims per KCNA

record.title: Two ballistic missiles launched near Pyongyang
record.detail: South Korea's JCS said two ballistic missiles were launched from near Pyongyang around 15:50, flying about 350 km toward the sea off the east coast; Japan reported an 80 km apogee.
record.attribution: JCS and Japan Ministry of Defence

record.title: About 10 ballistic missiles fired during Freedom Shield drills
record.detail: JCS and Japan's MoD reported about 10 ballistic missiles fired from the west coast around 13:34, flying about 340 km with 80 km apogee, during the US-ROK Freedom Shield exercise.
record.place: West coast (launch site not specified in source)
record.agency: ROK Joint Chiefs of Staff / Japan Ministry of Defence

record.title: SRBMs with cluster warheads fired from Sinpo
record.detail: Short-range ballistic missiles launched around 06:10 from the Sinpo area toward an island target about 136 km away. KCNA claimed five Hwasongpo-11-Ra missiles with cluster/mine warheads hit a target area (KCNA claim); Seoul called it a UNSC violation.
record.agency: ROK Ministry of National Defense; DPRK Missile Administration (per KCNA)
record.attribution: ROK MND, USINDOPACOM; KCNA claims attributed

record.title: Close-range ballistic missiles fired into Yellow Sea
record.detail: JCS said multiple close-range ballistic missiles and other projectiles were fired around 13:00 from Jongju toward the Yellow Sea; one flew about 80 km.

record.title: Destroyer Choe Hyon commissioned at Nampho
record.detail: State media (KCNA) reported the 5,000-ton destroyer Choe Hyon entered service at Nampho, with Kim Jong Un claiming no technological barriers to building destroyers and cruisers (KCNA claim).
record.attribution: KCNA as reported by USNI News

record.title: Seoul reports no DPRK GPS jamming near Baengnyeong in 2026
record.detail: An official of the Ministry of Science's Central Radio Management Service told NK News no North Korean GPS jamming had been observed near Baengnyeong Island so far in 2026, a break from past patterns.

record.title: Heavy rain warning for southern provinces
record.detail: North Korea's State Hydro-Meteorological Administration warned of 100-150 mm of rain in southern provinces overnight; KCNA said dredging and embankment work was intensified (state media claims via Yonhap).
record.attribution: DPRK state TV/KCNA as reported by Yonhap

record.title: Villages near Pyongsan uranium plant locked down over illness
record.detail: Daily NK source says villages near the Pyongsan uranium refinery were sealed from Jul 13 after residents showed hair loss, vomiting, skin blotches and lethargy; authorities chose lockdown over investigation. Unverified.
record.agency: WPK; North Hwanghae provincial committee; Ministry of Social Security

record.title: Two arrested in Wonsan for smishing and voice phishing
record.detail: Daily NK source says police (Ministry of Social Security) arrested two IT specialists in mid-July who sent fake bank/inspection texts and made fake intelligence-agency calls to extort wealthy traders in Wonsan, Sinuiju and Chongjin.
record.attribution: Anonymous Daily NK source (unverified; date mid-July approximate)

record.title: Unannounced Hwanggang Dam discharge on Imjin River
record.detail: South Korea's environment ministry detected by satellite around 20:47 that North Korea released water from Hwanggang Dam without notice; Seoul expressed regret and K-water opened all 7 Gunnam Dam gates.
record.agency: ROK Ministry of Climate, Energy and Environment; Ministry of Unification

record.title: Imjin River flood advisory downstream of DPRK dam
record.detail: Han River Flood Control Office issued a flood advisory as Pilseung Bridge reached 8.1 m (above 7.5 m threshold) after heavy rain and the unannounced Hwanggang release; residents told to evacuate riversides.

record.title: Bank-network hacking ring busted in Pyongyang
record.detail: Daily NK source says the National Intelligence Agency arrested ringleaders and IT staff on Jul 12 for siphoning funds from the Central Bank and Foreign Trade Bank into shell accounts. Unverified.

record.title: Bank-hacking ring laundered stolen funds via crypto
record.detail: Per Daily NK source, the busted ring converted state trade and foreign-currency funds into cryptocurrency and used Chinese brokers to cash out in dollars and yuan. Unverified.

record.title: Deadly gas station explosion in Sinuiju (early June)
record.detail: Daily NK source says a state-run gas station blast in Nagwon-dong in early June killed more than 20 people, including passengers of a waiting shuttle bus; authorities did not publicize it.
record.attribution: Anonymous Daily NK source (unverified; event early June)

record.title: 30+ private car accidents in North Phyongan in Q2
record.detail: Daily NK source says more than 30 private-vehicle accidents occurred in Sinuiju and nearby counties in April-June, mostly minor, many involving newly licensed drivers; no insurance or compensation system.

record.title: New Pyongwon apartment evacuated over collapse risk
record.detail: Daily NK source says a three-storey building passing inspection in late June showed collapse signs after rains; residents were evacuated before dawn in mid-July and a construction section chief was detained.

record.title: Cabinet emergency meeting on heat wave
record.detail: Daily NK source says the Cabinet met on Aug 2 over a heat wave since June and issued 20 heat guidelines (no midday outdoor labour, shifted hours, ice water).
record.agency: DPRK Cabinet; Ministry of Disaster Prevention
record.attribution: Anonymous Daily NK source in South Pyongan (unverified)

record.title: SRBM fired from Wonsan, first since April
record.detail: One short-range ballistic missile launched around 17:00 from the Wonsan area and fell in the Sea of Japan outside Japan's EEZ, per ROK MND and Japan's defense minister; ahead of Ulchi Freedom Shield.
record.agency: ROK Ministry of National Defense / Japan MoD

record.title: Late-July floods destroy homes in Singye county
record.detail: NK Pro satellite imagery analysis says late-July (Jul 20-23) floods, possibly after a Wangdang No. 2 Reservoir dam break, destroyed at least 380 homes, a market, roads and bridges near a military HQ in Singye; Ichon and Phangyo also hit.

record.title: Remittance broker fees exceed 50% amid crackdown
record.detail: Daily NK sources say illegal remittance fees now exceed 50% (minimum 5,000 yuan in Hoeryong); state security agents recently arrested a long-time Sinuiju broker.

record.title: Party orders rebuild of northern China border blockade
record.detail: Daily NK source says an Aug 10 party directive ordered border guards to rebury exposed landmines, keep shoot-on-sight orders and block civilian riverbank access along the China border.
record.agency: Workers' Party of Korea; border guard brigades
record.attribution: Anonymous Daily NK source in North Hamgyong (unverified)

record.title: Ballistic missile flies 700+ km from Wonsan
record.detail: JCS and Japan's MoD said a ballistic missile launched about 06:00 from the Wonsan area flew over 700 km; described as the 11th ballistic missile test of 2026.

record.title: About 100 heat deaths reported to Cabinet
record.detail: Daily NK source says the Ministry of Disaster Prevention told the Cabinet of about 100 heat deaths and about 4,300 heat illness cases since June 1. Unverified; no official DPRK figures.

record.title: Warning shots after DPRK soldiers cross MDL (eastern front)
record.detail: Per a government source cited by Yonhap, multiple North Korean soldiers crossed the MDL on the eastern front the previous week and returned after South Korean warning shots; first such warning shots of 2026.

record.title: 10+ short-range missiles fired from Pyongyang area
record.detail: More than 10 short-range ballistic missiles, identified by Seoul as 600mm KN-25 multiple rockets, flew about 300 km east as Ulchi Freedom Shield ended; Seoul called it a UNSC violation.

record.title: Heat wave triggers province-wide blackout in North Hwanghae
record.detail: Daily NK source says overheating transformers and substation failures caused a North Hwanghae-wide blackout, even cutting power to leader monuments; police and KPA units mobilized for repairs.

record.title: Chongjin hospital morgue fails in power outage
record.detail: Daily NK source says multi-day power shortages disabled morgue refrigeration at a Chongjin hospital, which cremated a body without family consent before Aug 8.

record.title: Sinuiju inundated as drainage fails
record.detail: Daily NK source says 379 mm fell in Sinuiju on Aug 24 (Kusong 408 mm), submerging single-storey homes in Sumun, Ryonsang and Ryonha; residents evacuated to shelters. Rain figures cited from state broadcaster/Rodong Sinmun.
record.attribution: Daily NK source; KCBS/Rodong Sinmun for rainfall

record.title: Record-scale downpour over North Phyongan
record.detail: State media figures cited by Daily NK: 379 mm in Sinuiju and 408 mm in Kusong on Aug 24, the region's highest.
record.attribution: State media as cited by Daily NK

record.title: Sinuiju-Dandong cargo trucking halted by flooding
record.detail: Daily NK source says cargo trucks between Dandong and Sinuiju were halted for over 48 hours from Aug 24 as flooding hit low-lying Apkang and Yokjon areas near the trade route.

record.title: Domestic money-transfer brokers return in Hyesan
record.detail: Daily NK source says private brokers moving cash between border and interior using coded phone talk are reviving as bank distrust grows, after earlier arrests by the National Intelligence Agency.

record.title: Power and water cut in flooded Sinuiju neighbourhood
record.detail: Daily NK source says electricity and water service remained cut in Sumun neighbourhood of Sinuiju as of Aug 26 after drainage failure flooding.

record.title: Cabinet orders crackdown on illegal Russian fuel trade
record.detail: Daily NK source says a Cabinet directive dated Aug 27 orders elimination of black-market Russian fuel by year-end, with punishment and asset confiscation for implicated officials.

record.title: Asset confiscation threatened in fuel black-market drive
record.detail: Daily NK source says the Cabinet's Aug 27 directive provides for confiscating assets of officials involved in illicit Russian fuel sales and seizing diverted fuel.

record.title: Repeated armed MDL crossings draw more warning shots
record.detail: JCS confirmed North Korean troops recently violated the MDL on the eastern front again and ROK forces fired warning shots; crossings involved armed patrol units.

record.title: Floods and landslides hit Rason near Russia border
record.detail: NK Pro imagery shows 100+ flooded homes in Kwangok-dong, landslides on roads and rail, and damaged bridges in Rason on Aug 31-Sep 1; state TV reported 266 mm of rain in a day.
record.attribution: NK Pro imagery; rainfall per DPRK state TV

record.title: Coal smuggled to China via ship-to-ship transfers off Nampo
record.detail: Daily NK source says over 3,000 tons of coal can be moved out in a night via ship-to-ship transfers near Nampo in breach of UN sanctions, at about 500 yuan/ton; volumes reportedly up 30-40% on last year.
record.attribution: Anonymous Daily NK source and Chinese traders (unverified)

record.title: Fake job-placement scam artist arrested in Sariwon
record.detail: Daily NK source says a former provincial party personnel official was arrested in mid-August for selling fake state job placements for USD 5,000-10,000+ per graduate using forged documents.

record.title: Second destroyer Kang Kon commissioned at Wonsan
record.detail: KCNA reported the 5,000-ton destroyer Kang Kon joined the East Sea Fleet; Kim Jong Un called it an offensive destroyer tied to nuclear deterrence (KCNA claim).
record.attribution: KCNA as reported by Korea Times

record.title: SRBMs and 600mm rockets fired from Wonsan
record.detail: JCS said multiple Hwasong-11 series missiles and 600mm rockets were fired from the Wonsan area around 05:20, flying about 250 km, a day after the Freedom Edge trilateral drill ended.

record.title: Coal mine shaft collapse buries three workers
record.detail: Daily NK source says timber supports gave way in an inclined shaft of a factory-run coal mine in North Hamgyong, burying three workers; one hospitalized with serious injuries.

record.title: Pork near record as African swine fever endemic
record.detail: Daily NK market survey puts pork at about 159,000 won/kg in August 2026, roughly 12x 2018 levels; analyst attributes it partly to endemic African swine fever since 2019.
record.attribution: Daily NK price survey; Good Farmers institute analyst

record.title: Man arrested for drone filming inside Kaesong homes
record.detail: Daily NK source says Kaesong security officials arrested a farm worker in late August for filming inside homes with a crop-spraying drone; the city then put all drone use under supervision.

record.title: Border meth prices surge under drug crackdown
record.detail: Daily NK source in North Pyongan says an intensified crackdown shrank distribution networks, with a meth dose now topping 500 yuan (about USD 75), up from 100-200 yuan.

record.title: Two ballistic missiles fired from Wonsan within three hours
record.detail: JCS detected a Hwasong-11 series missile around 15:00 flying about 450 km, followed by a second flying over 600 km; Seoul and Tokyo condemned the launches.
record.agency: ROK Joint Chiefs of Staff / Japan MoD

record.title: New Yalu River Bridge opening rumoured for early October
record.detail: Dandong traders cited by Daily NK say DPRK customs facilities at the long-idle New Yalu River Bridge are nearly complete, with opening talk around Oct 6-10; outlet cautions past rumours proved wrong.
record.attribution: Border traders via Daily NK source in China

record.title: Snow and gales cancel Jeju flights and ferries
record.detail: Heavy snow and wind advisories led to 17 flight cancellations and 29 delays at Jeju airport by 13:00, and six ferry services including Jeju–Wando and Jeju–Chuja were cancelled, per Korea Airports Corporation and KMA figures.
record.agency: Korea Airports Corporation; Korea Meteorological Administration
record.attribution: Korea JoongAng Daily citing Korea Airports Corporation and KMA

record.title: North Korea fires first ballistic missiles of 2026 from Pyongyang
record.detail: JCS detected multiple projectiles launched from Pyongyang's Ryokpho district flying about 900-950 km into the East Sea; North Korea claimed hypersonic missiles overseen by Kim Jong Un, per USNI News.
record.attribution: USNI News citing ROK JCS, KCNA and Japan MOD

record.title: North Korea says drone from Ganghwa crashed near Kaesong
record.detail: Pyongyang said a South Korean drone flew into its airspace on Jan 4, launched from Songhae township on Ganghwa Island and crashing in Kaepung District near Kaesong; Seoul denied military involvement and opened a joint military-police probe, per Korea Times.
record.attribution: Korea Times citing DPRK claims and ROK Ministry of National Defense

record.title: Black-ice crashes kill five on Seosan–Yeongdeok Expressway
record.detail: A series of black-ice crashes on the Sangju section before dawn killed five people, including four occupants of one sedan; police estimated more than 20 vehicles were involved and traffic was temporarily restricted.

record.title: Uiseong wildfire main blaze put out within three hours
record.detail: A wildfire broke out around 15:15 in Uiseong County; a Level 2 response was issued, residents were told to move to village halls, and 10 helicopters and 315 personnel contained it by about 18:00, per Korea Herald.
record.attribution: Korea Herald citing Gyeongbuk Fire Service Headquarters

record.title: Seoul city bus strike halts most of the fleet for two days
record.detail: The Seoul city bus union struck from 04:00 on Jan. 13, idling about 93% of the fleet (around 6,540 buses), until a deal late on Jan. 15 gave a 2.9% raise; service resumed the next morning. The city said emergency subway and shuttle measures cost about 10 billion won a day.
record.attribution: The Korea Herald; cost figure per Seoul city officials

record.title: Customs busts Chinese-run ring laundering 148.9 billion won via crypto
record.detail: Korea Customs Service said three Chinese nationals laundered about 148.9 billion won (~US$101.7 million) from 2021 to mid-2025 by buying crypto abroad, moving it through Korean wallets and cashing out via Korean bank accounts disguised as medical or tuition payments.
record.attribution: Korea Times citing Korea Customs Service

record.title: 73 Korean scam suspects repatriated from Cambodia
record.detail: 73 South Koreans were flown from Phnom Penh to Incheon on a Korean Air charter to face probes; police allege about 48.6 billion won (~US$33.6 million) was taken from about 869 victims via romance and investment scams run from seven identified compounds, per UPI.
record.attribution: UPI citing Korean National Police Agency

record.title: Probe raids NIS and Army Intelligence Command over drone flights into North
record.detail: A military-police joint task force searched 18 locations including the NIS and Army Intelligence Command; three active-duty officers were booked and three civilians charged over drones allegedly flown into North Korea, per UPI.

record.title: Hamyang wildfire burns 234 ha in 44 hours
record.detail: A wildfire that started around 21:00 burned 234 hectares in Hamyang County before being contained after about 44 hours; 164 residents evacuated. The Korea Forest Service raised a Level 2 response and 115 helicopters were mobilised.
record.agency: Korea Forest Service; National Fire Agency
record.attribution: The Korea Times citing the Korea Forest Service

record.title: Miryang wildfire burns 124 ha; 184 evacuated
record.detail: A wildfire that began about 16:00 in Miryang damaged at least 124 hectares and was 51% contained by the next morning; 184 people including care-hospital patients were evacuated and the National Fire Agency issued a national mobilization order.
record.agency: National Fire Agency / Korea Forest Service
record.attribution: Korea Herald citing National Fire Agency and Korea Forest Service

record.title: Ring smuggled 900,000 cigarette packs to Australia, NZ and UK
record.detail: Incheon customs referred 11 suspects over about 70 shipments of 900,000 packs (570,000 counterfeit) mislabelled as goods such as rubber mats, earning about 10 billion won (~US$6.78 million), per Korea Herald.
record.agency: Incheon Main Customs, Korea Customs Service
record.attribution: Korea Herald citing Korea Customs Service

record.title: Ultrafine dust alert as Chinese wildfire smoke reaches Seoul area
record.detail: A 'concern' level ultrafine dust disaster alert was issued at 17:00. Sunday with emergency reduction measures on Monday for the Seoul area and South Chungcheong as smoke from wildfires in northeast China drifted in, per Seoul Economic Daily citing NIER.
record.agency: Ministry of Climate, Energy and Environment / NIER
record.attribution: Seoul Economic Daily citing National Institute of Environmental Research

record.title: FIU fines Bithumb 36.8 billion won over AML breaches
record.detail: The Financial Intelligence Unit fined crypto exchange Bithumb 36.8 billion won (~US$24.6 million) for about 6.65 million AML violations including KYC failures, and ordered a six-month partial suspension for new users; a court later lifted the suspension.
record.attribution: CoinDesk citing Korea Financial Intelligence Unit

record.title: Signal failure halts Line 9 express trains
record.detail: A signal failure detected at 10:22 forced all Seoul Subway Line 9 express trains to run as local services for about two hours until 12:17; the cause was under investigation.
record.attribution: Korea JoongAng Daily citing the operator

record.title: Daejeon auto parts factory fire kills 14, injures 60
record.detail: Fire broke out around 13:17 at an auto parts plant in Daedeok District, killing 14 and injuring 60; nine victims were found in an illegally built rest area and police, NFS and the labor ministry are investigating the cause.
record.agency: Daejeon Metropolitan Police Agency / National Fire Agency
record.attribution: Korea JoongAng Daily citing fire and police authorities

record.title: Three civilians indicted over drone incursion into North Korea
record.detail: Seoul Central District Prosecutors' Office indicted three civilians linked to a drone company for 'general benefiting of the enemy' and Aviation Safety Act violations over drone flights into the North, per NK News.

record.title: President Lee expresses regret to North over January drone incursion
record.detail: President Lee Jae Myung expressed regret to North Korea for tensions caused by the January drone flight after Seoul's probe found NIS officials and an active-duty officer were involved, per Malay Mail.

record.title: Gale-force winds batter Jeju; KMA records 28.9 m/s on Udo
record.detail: KMA recorded winds of 28.9 m/s on Udo and 27.2 m/s at Jeju airport; high-wave warnings halted island ferries and 20-30 mm/h rain was forecast into the next morning, per The Star.

record.title: 246 flights cancelled at Jeju airport, 3,000+ stranded
record.detail: By 19:00 246 flights (12 international) were cancelled and 83 delayed at Jeju International Airport due to strong winds, stranding over 3,000 passengers; island ferries were also suspended.

record.title: FIU fines Coinone 5.2 billion won, partial suspension
record.detail: The FIU fined exchange Coinone 5.2 billion won (~US$3.49 million) for failing to verify about 70,000 users and facilitating around 10,000 transactions with 16 unregistered overseas exchanges, plus a three-month partial suspension.
record.attribution: Korea Herald citing Korea Financial Intelligence Unit

record.title: Laotian worker arrested over 5 kg meth shipped from Thailand
record.detail: Customs' Gwangju office arrested a Lao national who received 5 kg of methamphetamine hidden in snack and coffee bags shipped from Thailand to Yongin in February; the alleged ringleader remains at large.
record.attribution: Korea Herald citing Korea Customs Service

record.title: FX task force uncovers 600 billion won in illegal transactions incl. hwanchigi
record.detail: A government-wide illegal FX response team (NIS, NTS, BOK, FSS) uncovered over 600 billion won in four months, including a remittance firm using 25,000 virtual accounts to launder gambling proceeds (400 billion won) and a used-car exporter paid in crypto cashed out via hwanchigi brokers (200 billion won).
record.attribution: Kyunghyang Shinmun citing government FX response team

record.title: Korean man with disability freed from Sihanoukville captivity
record.detail: A Korean man in his 30s with a disability, lured by a social-media job post, was held in a Sihanoukville hotel, abused and threatened with a US$20,000 ransom; he was freed on May 7, per Korean National Police Agency.
record.agency: Korean National Police Agency / Korea-Cambodia Korean Desk
record.attribution: Korea Times citing Korean National Police Agency

record.title: Korean Desk rescues woman held for ransom in Phnom Penh
record.detail: The Korea-Cambodia joint police task force (Korean Desk) rescued a Korean woman in her 20s held captive after travelling to meet an online contact, and arrested a Chinese suspect, per KNPA.
record.agency: Korean National Police Agency / Korea-Cambodia Korean Desk
record.attribution: Korea JoongAng Daily citing Korean National Police Agency

record.title: Earliest-ever heat-related death recorded in Seoul
record.detail: KDCA reported a man in Seoul died of heat-related illness on May 16, the earliest such case on record, a day after it began surveillance at 516 emergency rooms; seven heat patients were treated the previous day.
record.agency: Korea Disease Control and Prevention Agency

record.title: 24 African swine fever farm cases confirmed in seven provinces
record.detail: The agriculture ministry confirmed 24 ASF cases between Jan 16 and Mar 16 across seven provinces including Gyeonggi (Pocheon, Yeoncheon) and Gangwon; standstill orders were lifted Apr 22 but alerts remain for 32 cities and counties.
record.agency: Ministry of Agriculture, Food and Rural Affairs
record.attribution: Korea Times citing Ministry of Agriculture, Food and Rural Affairs

record.title: Overpass under demolition collapses in Seodaemun, 3 dead
record.detail: A section of a 1966-built overpass being demolished in Seoul's Seodaemun District gave way, killing three workers and injuring three; debris fell on nearby tracks, per AP via ABC News.
record.attribution: AP citing fire and police officials

record.title: Korail suspends some Seoul Station services after overpass collapse
record.detail: Korea Railroad Corp. suspended some operations into Seoul Station after debris from a collapsed overpass fell onto tracks in Seodaemun District; local roads were sealed off.

record.title: Soil collapse kills worker at Gangnam sewer site
record.detail: A 3.5-metre pile of soil collapsed at a sewer maintenance site near Suseo Station, killing a worker in his 60s; a labour office official said no retaining wall had been installed.
record.attribution: The Korea Herald citing a labour office official

record.title: Cambodian court jails six Chinese for life over scam-linked killing of Korean student
record.detail: Kampot Provincial Court sentenced six Chinese nationals to life for murder, unlawful detention, torture and organised fraud over the 2025 death of a Korean university student lured to Cambodia by a scam ring, per Korea Times.

record.title: Explosion at Hanwha Aerospace Daejeon plant kills five
record.detail: An explosion at 10:59 while workers cleaned explosive residue from rocket-propellant tooling killed five and injured two; the cause was under investigation and executives could face probes under the Serious Accidents Punishment Act.
record.agency: National Fire Agency; Ministry of Employment and Labor
record.attribution: The Korea Times citing police, fire authorities and the company

record.title: Tropical Storm Jangmi disrupts Incheon and Gimpo flights
record.detail: AirHelp flight data showed 20 cancellations and 120 delays at Incheon and 12 cancellations and 48 delays at Gimpo on June 3 as Tropical Storm Jangmi affected the region.

record.title: 23 charged for laundering Cambodia phishing proceeds via USDT
record.detail: Seoul police referred 23 suspects (two detained) for laundering about 16.8 billion won (~US$11.1 million) for a Cambodia-based phishing group by cycling USDT through domestic and overseas exchanges; the alleged ringleader is under an Interpol Red Notice, per Decrypt.
record.attribution: Decrypt citing Seoul Metropolitan Police Agency

record.title: Nationwide Japanese encephalitis alert after virus found in Daegu mosquito
record.detail: KDCA issued a nationwide Japanese encephalitis alert after detecting the virus in a Culex mosquito in Daegu, earlier than last year's Aug 1 alert, and urged local larval control.
record.agency: Korea Disease Control and Prevention Agency

record.title: Car mounts Busan sidewalk, killing two pedestrians
record.detail: A car driven by a man in his 70s struck four pedestrians on a sidewalk in Nam District, killing two women and injuring two; police said the driver claimed sudden unintended acceleration and the cause was under investigation.

record.title: Trawler Dong-a No. 3 collides with gas carrier off Busan
record.detail: The 79-ton trawler collided with a gas carrier about 24 nautical miles southeast of Daebyeon Port, Gijang; five of eight crew were rescued, one died and two were missing. Oceans Minister Hwang Jong-woo ordered an all-out search.
record.agency: Ulsan Coast Guard; Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries
record.attribution: The Herald Business citing the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries

record.title: Over 10 Chinese and Russian military aircraft enter KADIZ
record.detail: JCS said more than 10 Chinese and Russian military aircraft entered and left the KADIZ over the East Sea and off the south coast during an apparent joint drill without violating territorial airspace; ROK fighters were scrambled.

record.title: WeTax and Gov24 local tax services down for 12 hours
record.detail: The Interior Ministry said a surge in data traffic during a system update knocked out WeTax, Gov24, civil-service kiosks and the local tax network for about 12 hours; services were restored by 20:50 and tax deadlines were extended.
record.agency: Ministry of the Interior and Safety
record.attribution: Korea JoongAng Daily citing the Ministry of the Interior and Safety

record.title: M2.1 quake near Gimcheon felt in two provinces
record.detail: KMA reported a magnitude 2.1 earthquake 13 km northeast of Gimcheon at 9 km depth, with max intensity III in North Gyeongsang; no significant damage reported.

record.title: First repatriation of Korean scam members from Malaysia
record.detail: Two Korean members of a Malaysia-based 'no-show' fraud ring were arrested at Kuala Lumpur International Airport on July 7 and repatriated, the first such case from Malaysia, per Seoul Economic Daily.

record.title: Power failure paralyses Seoul Subway Line 1 at rush hour
record.detail: A power outage at 07:29 halted southbound Line 1 trains between Changdong and Sinimun; power returned at 09:48 and service at 09:57, causing heavy congestion along the line. Korail said the cause was under investigation.

record.title: Monsoon downpours hit Chungcheong; one missing, 758 evacuated
record.detail: Heavy rain on July 9-10 dropped 267.1 mm on Cheonan and 259 mm on Gyeryong; a man in his 70s was swept away in Yeongju, 758 people were evacuated nationwide and over 450 facilities damaged, per the Central Disaster and Safety Countermeasures Headquarters.
record.agency: Central Disaster and Safety Countermeasures Headquarters
record.attribution: Korea JoongAng Daily citing Central Disaster and Safety Countermeasures Headquarters

record.title: Five landslides in North Chungcheong and Gangwon during monsoon rain
record.detail: Five landslides were reported in North Chungcheong and eastern Gangwon during July 9-10 rain, with no casualties, per the disaster headquarters.
record.agency: Central Disaster and Safety Countermeasures Headquarters
record.attribution: Korea JoongAng Daily citing Central Disaster and Safety Countermeasures Headquarters

record.title: Man in his 70s swept away by rapid current in Yeongju
record.detail: A man in his 70s went missing after being swept away by a fast-flowing stream in Yeongju during heavy rain, per disaster authorities.
record.agency: Central Disaster and Safety Countermeasures Headquarters
record.attribution: Korea JoongAng Daily citing Central Disaster and Safety Countermeasures Headquarters

record.title: Heavy rain blocks Dongbu Expressway entrance in Seoul
record.detail: Overnight rain of 117.9 mm in Seoul and over 150 mm in northern Gyeonggi blocked the entrance to the Dongbu Expressway; the Korea Forest Service issued landslide warnings for the whole Greater Seoul area at 06:00.
record.agency: Korea Meteorological Administration; Korea Forest Service
record.attribution: The Korea Herald citing KMA and the Korea Forest Service

record.title: Torrential rain floods Seoul, Gyeonggi and Daegu
record.detail: Overnight rain reached 166 mm in Eunpyeong (64.5 mm/h in Seodaemun) and 183.5 mm in Daegu's Jisan-dong; Seoul issued flood warnings for Gangseo, Eunpyeong and Mapo, and people were rescued from flooded homes in Paju and Gumi and stranded vehicles in Daegu.
record.agency: Seoul Metropolitan Government; Korea Meteorological Administration; Korea Forest Service
record.attribution: Korea JoongAng Daily citing KMA, Seoul city and the Korea Forest Service

record.title: Rain triggers 540 landslides and rockfalls; one missing in Yeongwol
record.detail: Up to 197.5 mm in Paju and 171.1 mm in Cheorwon caused 793 facility damage cases including 540 landslides and rockfalls; 294 people were in shelters and a fisher went missing in the Jucheon River in Yeongwol, per the disaster headquarters.
record.agency: Central Disaster and Safety Countermeasures Headquarters
record.attribution: Korea JoongAng Daily citing the Central Disaster and Safety Countermeasures Headquarters

record.title: Customs seizes record 1,007 kg of drugs in first half
record.detail: Korea Customs Service caught 767 smuggling cases totaling 1,007 kg in H1 2026 (654 kg cannabis, 230 kg meth, 58 kg ketamine), with Thailand the top origin; 717 offenders were caught including 14 teenagers.
record.attribution: Korea JoongAng Daily citing Korea Customs Service

record.title: Customs uncovers 7.2 trillion won in illegal FX dealings in H1
record.detail: Korea Customs Service said it uncovered 792 illegal foreign-exchange cases worth 7.2 trillion won (~US$4.9 billion) in H1 2026, including unauthorised transfers, hidden overseas assets and export proceeds received in crypto.
record.attribution: Korea JoongAng Daily citing Korea Customs Service

record.title: Miryang restricts supply at 39 of 40 farm reservoirs
record.detail: Miryang moved 39 of its 40 agricultural reservoirs to every-other-day supply; Maheul and Baegan reservoirs were near empty and Miryang Dam was at 34.6%, per Seoul Economic Daily citing Korea Rural Community Corporation.
record.attribution: Seoul Economic Daily citing Korea Rural Community Corporation

record.title: 50-metre section of Pohang sea bridge collapses
record.detail: About 50 metres of the 225-metre Boritdol pedestrian sea bridge in Guryongpo-eup fell into the sea; all 17 anglers on it were rescued within 12 minutes. The bridge had been repaired in 2025–26 but was not subject to mandatory safety inspections.

record.title: Unmun Dam at 27.3% as drought exposes submerged village
record.detail: Unmun Dam storage stood at 27.3%, exposing a village submerged for 41 years; North Gyeongsang reservoirs averaged 58.2% against a normal 71.6%, and Miryang's Baekan Reservoir held about 1.2%.

record.title: Bohyeonsan Dam storage falls to 16.4% as southern drought worsens
record.detail: The National Drought Information Portal put Bohyeonsan Dam storage at 16.4% amid prolonged heat and below-average rain across southern regions, per Korea Herald.
record.attribution: Korea Herald citing National Drought Information Portal

record.title: Ulsan's Daegok Dam falls to 8.1%; river water piped in
record.detail: Daegok Dam fell to 8.1% of capacity and Ulsan began drawing water from the Nakdong River 40 km away; Miryang and Changnyeong began supply restrictions and Cheongdo stockpiled bottled water.

record.title: National record 42.5C set in Yangsan
record.detail: KMA confirmed 42.5C in Yangsan at 13:26, the highest temperature on record in Korea; Yangsan exceeded 40C five days running and more than 20 localities were under the new emergency heat alert, per ABC News.

record.title: Record 186 heat-illness cases in a day; two suspected deaths in Wanju
record.detail: KDCA logged 186 heat-related illness cases on Aug 3, the year's daily high, bringing the total to 2,221 with 19 suspected deaths; two elderly people with underlying conditions died in Wanju, per Korea Herald.
record.agency: Korea Disease Control and Prevention Agency
record.attribution: Korea Herald citing KDCA and KMA

record.title: Heat-driven apartment blackouts hit Incheon, Goyang, Seoul
record.detail: Overloaded transformers and wiring amid the heat wave cut power to 374 households in Gyeyang, Incheon for over four hours and 460 in Deogyang, Goyang for two hours, with outages also in Gangseo, Seoul and Suwon, per JoongAng Daily.
record.attribution: Korea JoongAng Daily citing local authorities

record.title: First SFTS death of 2026 reported on Jeju
record.detail: Korea reported its first severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome (tick-borne) death of 2026 on Jeju on Aug 5; Seoul expanded tick surveillance and found no SFTS virus in about 480 ticks, per Korea Times.
record.agency: Korea Disease Control and Prevention Agency
record.attribution: Korea Times citing Seoul Research Institute of Public Health and Environment

record.title: North Korea fires SRBM from Wonsan toward East Sea
record.detail: JCS said it detected a short-range ballistic missile launched from the Wonsan area around 17:00; it was the first known SRBM test in about five months, per NK News.

record.title: 81 mm/h downpour floods Gangneung roads
record.detail: A cloudburst of 81.4 mm/h in Gangneung's Yonggang-dong briefly submerged roads; seven vacationers were rescued near Baekdamsa in Inje and a multi-vehicle crash near Daegwallyeong Tunnel injured three. Gangneung raised its disaster headquarters to Level 2.
record.attribution: The Kyunghyang Shinmun citing KMA and Gangneung City

record.title: Crow contact causes back-to-back outages in Busan's Buk District
record.detail: About 986 households in Hwamyeong- and Geumgok-dong lost power on Aug 8 and 981 in Gupo-dong on Aug 9 for about an hour each; Busan city blamed a crow touching equipment, per JoongAng Daily.
record.attribution: Korea JoongAng Daily citing Busan city and KEPCO

record.title: Three rescued after motorboat capsizes off Ongjin
record.detail: Incheon Coast Guard rescued three men clinging to a capsized 0.28-ton motorboat near Choji Island about 11 hours after they lost contact on a fishing trip; all were stable.
record.attribution: Korea Herald citing Incheon Coast Guard

record.title: Okcheon Reservoir surface shrinks 89% in drought
record.detail: Satellite imagery showed Okcheon Reservoir in Changnyeong down 88.8% in surface area from a year earlier; agricultural reservoirs averaged 53.2% nationwide and 39.6% in South Gyeongsang as of Aug. 3, and water trucks were supplying farms.
record.attribution: Korea JoongAng Daily; satellite figures from analyst TelePIX
record.value_unit: % avg agricultural reservoir storage, South Gyeongsang

record.title: Typhoon Chan-hom to bring east-coast rain but no direct hit
record.detail: KMA said Typhoon Chan-hom (No. 15), near Tokyo, would not directly affect Korea but easterly flow could bring 20-60 mm to the east coast and 10-40 mm to South Gyeongsang on Aug 12-13, likely insufficient to ease the southern drought.

record.title: Philippines-based ring used porn sites to drive 4.7 trillion won in illegal bets
record.detail: Seoul police detained two men accused of running a Pasay City-based network whose own illegal pornography sites funnelled users to 18 gambling sites, with 4.7 trillion won wagered and 47.6 billion won (~US$34 million) in profits since 2019.
record.attribution: Korea Herald citing Seoul Metropolitan Police Agency

record.title: Miryang, Geoje and Haman hit 'severe' drought stage
record.detail: Seoul Economic Daily reported Miryang, Geoje and Haman reached the severe drought stage, with agricultural drought alerts in 17 of 18 South Gyeongsang municipalities, reservoirs at 33.3% (normal 71.3%) and about 2,121 ha of crops affected; water was rationed in 26 villages.
record.agency: National Fire Agency / South Gyeongsang Province

record.title: Bangkok-based sextortion phishing ring busted
record.detail: Seoul police with Thai police apprehended 11 members of a Bangkok call centre that impersonated officials and extorted 68 Koreans with nude photos, taking 6.7 billion won (~US$4.73 million); nine Korean members remain at large in Thailand.
record.attribution: Korea JoongAng Daily citing Seoul Metropolitan Police Agency

record.title: 159 fire tankers mobilized to supply water to drought-hit South Gyeongsang
record.detail: Fire authorities extended a national mobilization order, sending 159 water tankers (100 from other provinces) that delivered 12,445 tons in two days; provincial reservoir storage averaged 32.2% versus a 70.6% norm, per Korea Times.
record.agency: National Fire Agency / Ministry of the Interior and Safety
record.attribution: Korea Times citing fire authorities and interior ministry

record.title: Scaffolding contact cuts power to 251 Mapo households
record.detail: A power line contacted by construction scaffolding cut electricity to 251 households in Seogyo-dong at 18:52 during the heat wave; KEPCO partly restored supply by 19:41.

record.title: Record deluge in Geoje and Tongyeong triggers floods and landslides
record.detail: Three-day rain from Aug 16 reached 851.1 mm in Geoje (124.5 mm in one hour) and 704.8 mm in Tongyeong; one person died, four were injured, about 160 evacuated and 136 rescued by firefighters, per Korea Herald. A landslide engulfed the first floor of an apartment building in Okpo-dong, Geoje.
record.attribution: Korea Herald citing KMA and fire authorities

record.title: Warning shots after North Korean soldiers cross MDL on eastern front
record.detail: The South Korean military fired warning shots after multiple North Korean soldiers crossed the Military Demarcation Line on the eastern front the previous week; they returned north. It was the first such warning fire of 2026, per Korea Herald.

record.title: Landslide hits apartment building in Okpo-dong, Geoje
record.detail: During the southeastern deluge a landslide engulfed the first floor of an apartment building in Okpo-dong around 04:32; multiple other landslides blocked roads, per Korea Herald.

record.title: Coast guard: 31 Chinese caught entering illegally via Taean coast since 2019
record.detail: The Coast Guard said 31 Chinese nationals were caught entering by small or rubber boats at Taean between Sept 2019 and May 2026, 25 of them previously deported workers; attempts peak in calm seas in spring and autumn.
record.attribution: Korea JoongAng Daily citing Korea Coast Guard

record.title: Police and China bust China-based voice phishing ring
record.detail: Gangwon police with Jilin public security arrested 10 (6 Korean, 4 Chinese) accused of taking about 10 billion won (~US$7.23 million) from 118 mostly elderly Koreans in 2025-26 by impersonating officials and planting malicious apps; proceeds were split in crypto.
record.attribution: Korea Times citing Gangwon Provincial Police Agency

record.title: Chungbuk police bust Vietnam-based gambling site with 63 billion won in bets
record.detail: Chungbuk police referred 13 operators and 105 users of a Vietnam-run baccarat, slots and sports-betting site that took 63 billion won (~US$46 million) in bets from 3,553 users; 186.35 million won was frozen and a ringleader is at large.
record.attribution: Korea JoongAng Daily citing Chungbuk Provincial Police Agency

record.title: Heat-related illnesses near 3,800 with 34 deaths
record.detail: KDCA surveillance counted nearly 3,800 heat-related illness cases and 34 deaths this summer as of Aug 27, led by Gyeonggi (925), Seoul (457) and South Gyeongsang (322); level-4 heat risk alert remained in effect.
record.agency: Korea Disease Control and Prevention Agency

record.title: KMA: Krovanh expected to stall near Okinawa; fall typhoon risk rising
record.detail: KMA said Typhoon Krovanh (No. 24) should be pushed back by high pressure north of Korea; no typhoon hit Korea in summer 2026 despite 17 forming nearby, and experts warned fall paths toward Korea could open, per JoongAng Daily.

record.title: Tugboat capsizes off Busan; one dead, six missing
record.detail: The 286-ton tugboat TNS Catcher capsized about 9 km southeast of Oryukdo with eight crew; one Indonesian crew member was rescued, one Korean crew member was found dead and six were missing. The Busan Coast Guard deployed 13 vessels and President Lee Jae Myung ordered all resources mobilised.
record.attribution: The Korea Herald citing the Busan Coast Guard

record.title: Typhoon Krovanh winds delay 84 Jeju flights, halt ferries
record.detail: Wind shear and high-wind advisories linked to Typhoon Krovanh delayed 84 of 505 scheduled flights at Jeju airport; ferries to Jindo and Samcheonpo and all services to Gapado and Marado were suspended, per the Jeju weather office and Korea Airports Corporation.
record.agency: Korea Airports Corporation; Jeju Regional Office of Meteorology
record.attribution: Seoul Economic Daily citing Korea Airports Corporation and the Jeju weather office

record.title: Typhoon Krovanh gales kill one at Jeju Port
record.detail: Gales from Typhoon Krovanh reached 26.9 m/s at Saebyeol Oreum; a man in his 50s died when a crane collapsed at Jeju Port and others were hurt, 184 flights were delayed and island ferries suspended, per Herald Business.
record.attribution: Herald Business citing KMA, coast guard and fire authorities

record.title: North Korean troops crossed MDL more than 20 times in a month
record.detail: JCS said North Korean troops crossed the MDL over 20 times in the past month, mostly on one eastern-front section during DMZ construction work, exceeding 17 in all of 2025; the military fired warning shots and asked the UN Command to investigate.
record.agency: ROK Joint Chiefs of Staff / UN Command
record.attribution: Korea JoongAng Daily citing JCS and UNC

record.title: First human Japanese encephalitis case of 2026 confirmed
record.detail: KDCA confirmed the year's first Japanese encephalitis case in an unvaccinated woman in her 60s who fell ill around Aug 15, warning September-October is peak season, per Seoul Economic Daily.
record.agency: Korea Disease Control and Prevention Agency

record.title: North Korea fires several ballistic missiles from Wonsan
record.detail: JCS detected several ballistic missiles launched from the Wonsan area around 05:20 that flew about 250 km, a day after US-ROK-Japan maritime drills ended, per Al Jazeera.

record.title: Gyeonggi police bust shell-company laundering ring for fraud gangs
record.detail: Gyeonggi Nambu police arrested seven, including the ringleader, accused of laundering 93.4 billion won (~US$67 million) in fraud proceeds from mid-2024 to Feb 2026 through fake gift-certificate distributors in Seoul and Gyeonggi.
record.attribution: Korea JoongAng Daily citing Gyeonggi Nambu Provincial Police Agency

record.title: 15 ground-subsidence cases on Seoul roads so far in 2026
record.detail: MOLIT's underground safety information system logged 15 sinkhole cases in Seoul through Sept. 15, after 42 in 2025; about 40% of 2021–2025 cases were linked to sewer damage. Recent holes opened near Suyu and Gongdeok stations and in Jegi-dong without injuries.
record.agency: Ministry of Land, Infrastructure and Transport
record.attribution: Seoul Economic Daily citing MOLIT data

record.title: Ministry tightens winter controls on bird flu, FMD and ASF
record.detail: MAFRA said 21 of 2026's 24 ASF cases were linked to contaminated plasma-protein feed, overseas wild-bird flu cases doubled to 2,957, and a new SAT1 FMD strain is in China and Mongolia; 280 control zones will run Oct-Feb.
record.agency: Ministry of Agriculture, Food and Rural Affairs
record.attribution: Korea JoongAng Daily citing Ministry of Agriculture, Food and Rural Affairs

record.title: 462 Koreans arrested in six Southeast Asian countries in H1; rings shift to Malaysia
record.detail: Foreign ministry data showed 462 Koreans arrested for transnational crimes in six Southeast Asian countries in H1 2026, 4.6 times the prior year; rings have moved to Malaysia, Thailand, Vietnam and Kazakhstan, incl. a Bac Ninh ring that took about 24.3 billion won from 630+ small-business owners.
record.attribution: Seoul Economic Daily citing Ministry of Foreign Affairs

record.title: 30 arrested in ring hiding meth in sunflower-seed packets
record.detail: Seoul police arrested 30 (17 detained) over drugs worth about 6 billion won (~US$4.3 million), including 1.25 kg meth and 500 g ketamine smuggled from Cambodia, the Philippines and Thailand via Incheon airport; three overseas leaders are on Interpol red notices.
record.attribution: Seoul Economic Daily citing Seoul Metropolitan Police Agency

record.title: Contaminated tank cuts water to ~5,000 Suwon apartments
record.detail: Tap water smelling of paint thinner cut supply to about 5,000 households in a Jangan-gu apartment complex for over 12 hours; management blamed epoxy waterproofing work on the tank and the city sent water tankers.
record.attribution: SBS News citing apartment management and district officials

record.title: North Korea fires two projectiles from Wonsan within three hours
record.detail: JCS detected an SRBM (possibly Hwasong-11 type) from the Wonsan area around 15:00 that flew about 450 km, and a second projectile around 18:00; it followed a Sept 12 launch, per JoongAng Daily.
record.attribution: Korea JoongAng Daily citing ROK JCS

record.title: Workers at three Korail subsidiaries begin three-day strike
record.detail: About 1,300 workers at Korail Networks, Korail Tourism Development and the railway customer centre struck against a plan to merge five subsidiaries into three, according to the union (police estimated 800 at the rally). No major train cancellations were reported in the article.
record.attribution: SBS News; turnout per union, rally figure per police estimate

record.title: Apartment fire in Gangnam's Suseo-dong forces 60 to evacuate
record.detail: A fire at an apartment building in Suseo-dong around 12:10 forced 60 residents to evacuate and one was treated for smoke inhalation; about 200 firefighters put it out in 1 hour 20 minutes, per SBS.

record.title: Chuseok traffic: Seoul–Busan trip over 7 hours
record.detail: Korea Expressway Corp. estimated 6.84 million vehicles on the roads on Chuseok day; at 14:00. Busan to Seoul took 8 hours 10 minutes and Seoul to Busan 7 hours 20 minutes. Tolls were waived Sept. 24–27.
record.attribution: The Korea Times citing Korea Expressway Corp.

record.title: Bird contact cuts power to 578 Yangju households
record.detail: A bird touching high-voltage equipment caused an outage in Samsung-dong and Mansong-dong around 11:00; KEPCO restored power in about an hour.

record.title: Sinkhole in Xaythany leaves four missing
record.detail: A large sinkhole opened in Thongmang village; four people were missing and presumed dead, and the search was ended on 15 Jan after the Department of Geology and Minerals said the ground was highly unstable. Authorities pledged an investigation into the cause.
record.attribution: Department of Geology and Minerals and Xaythany District Administration, via The Nation

record.title: January road toll: 113 dead in 801 crashes
record.detail: The Traffic Police Department reported 801 road accidents in January 2026 with 113 deaths and 1,149 injuries; Vientiane Capital had the most (128 crashes, 27 deaths).
record.attribution: Traffic Police Department, Ministry of Public Security, via Laotian Times

record.title: Nearly 2,800 arrested in Golden Triangle SEZ since 2023, officials say
record.detail: At a Lao-Chinese security meeting, officials said nearly 2,800 suspects of 27 nationalities had been arrested in the Golden Triangle SEZ since 2023, plus 396 in 18 operations elsewhere in Bokeo; the GTSEZ police unit has been under direct Ministry of Public Security supervision since March 2023.
record.attribution: Ministry of Public Security officials, via Laotian Times

record.title: UXO: 7 casualties in two 2026 incidents so far
record.detail: Bernama reported 2 UXO incidents with 7 casualties so far in 2026 (25 casualties in 15 accidents in 2025), with President Thongloun Sisoulith urging faster clearance; a 113 kg bomb was removed in Huay Pan village, Luang Prabang, on 7 Jan.
record.attribution: Lao officials incl. President Thongloun Sisoulith, via Bernama

record.title: Bank of Lao PDR tightens offshore account rules
record.detail: BOL Decision No. 251/BOL requires prior central bank approval for most Lao residents opening offshore bank accounts, with account activity reportable to the BOL on request.
record.attribution: Bank of the Lao PDR decision, summarised by VDB Loi

record.title: PM2.5 exceeds 100 µg/m3 in several provinces
record.detail: The Ministry of Agriculture and Environment reported PM2.5 of 123 µg/m3 in Champasak and above 100 µg/m3 in Luang Prabang, Salavan and Attapeu (standard 50), and called for tighter burning controls and faster fire detection.
record.attribution: Ministry of Agriculture and Environment, via Xinhua

record.title: 16,000+ fire hotspots; AQI over 200 in the north
record.detail: The Ministry of Agriculture and Environment reported 16,395 hotspots in Q1 2026 (895 on 1 Apr alone) with AQI above 200 in Bokeo, Oudomxay and Luang Prabang, and urged masks and avoiding outdoor exercise.
record.attribution: Ministry of Agriculture and Environment, via Laotian Times

record.title: Overnight Pakse-Vientiane bus overturns, 8 dead
record.detail: An overnight bus from Pakse to Vientiane carrying 48 people overturned on a curve near Nam Duea village at about 04:20; authorities blamed wet roads and speeding. Eight died, including a foreigner, and 35 were injured.
record.attribution: Bolikhamxay provincial authorities, via Laotian Times

record.title: EDL schedules three days of daytime outages in Vientiane
record.detail: Electricité du Laos cut power for 5-9 hours on 24-26 April in Nongbone, Chanthabouly's Phontong area and Sibounhueang and Hongkaikeo villages for equipment installation and relocation of 18 poles for road works.

record.title: APG follow-up keeps Laos partially compliant on higher-risk countries
record.detail: The Asia/Pacific Group on Money Laundering published Laos' 2nd enhanced follow-up report: Recommendation 19 stays Partially Compliant despite progress, with 16 of 40 FATF Recommendations rated C/LC.

record.title: 230 detained in Bokeo call-centre scam raids
record.detail: Bokeo provincial police said operations on 4-11 May in Houayxay (71) and Tonpheung (159) districts detained 230 suspects, including 106 Lao, 62 Chinese, 52 Myanmar, 5 Philippine, 4 Malaysian and 1 Indonesian nationals.
record.attribution: Bokeo Provincial Public Security Office, via KPL

record.title: 10.4 million meth pills and 1.2 t crystal meth seized in Vientiane
record.detail: Xaythany police said coordinated pre-dawn raids across Xaythany, Hadxaifong and Naxaythong districts seized 10.4 million methamphetamine pills, 1,235 kg crystal meth and 6.5 kg heroin, arresting five suspects.
record.attribution: Xaythany District Police, via Laotian Times

record.title: 135 detained in Boten SEZ scam operation
record.detail: Police detained 135 suspects in an operation in the Boten Special Economic Zone on the China border, part of a July-wide crackdown in which the Ministry of Public Security reported 1,044 detentions.
record.attribution: Ministry of Public Security, via Laotian Times

record.title: Laos reports 4,025 drug arrests in first half of 2026
record.detail: Prime Minister Sonexay Siphandone told the National Assembly that authorities handled 1,786 drug cases and arrested 4,025 suspects in H1 2026; reported seizures included 1.5 tonnes of meth tablets and 500 kg crystal meth in Vientiane Province in April and 300 kg crystal meth in Khammouane in July.
record.agency: Lao Government / Ministry of Public Security
record.attribution: Prime Minister Sonexay Siphandone (National Assembly report), via Laotian Times

record.title: 122 foreigners arrested in Sisattanak scam raid
record.detail: Vientiane police and immigration raided houses in Sisattanak district, detaining 122 people including 34 Chinese, 26 Brazilians and 19 Malaysians; the report lists further arrests of 28-174 people in operations on 3-8 July including at Boten and in Champasak.
record.attribution: Vientiane Capital Police, via Laotian Times

record.title: Public Security order bars landlords and hotels from hosting scam operations
record.detail: A Ministry of Public Security order prohibits individuals, businesses, hotels and landlords from providing premises or support to scam or illegal gambling operations, with fines, confiscated deposits and prosecution for violators and sanctions for officials who assist; it notes 4,482 cybercrime arrests in H1 2026.
record.attribution: Ministry of Public Security, via Laotian Times

record.title: Week-long heavy rain warning for eight provinces
record.detail: The Department of Meteorology and Hydrology warned of heavy to very heavy rain nationwide with risk of flash floods and landslides, singling out Phongsaly, Xieng Khuang, Xaysomboun, Bolikhamxay, Khammuan, Savannakhet, Champasak and Attapeu; a Savannakhet tributary was reported above its 8 m warning level.
record.attribution: Department of Meteorology and Hydrology (Ministry of Agriculture and Environment), via Xinhua

record.title: 261 detained in Thatluang Lake SEZ raid
record.detail: Vientiane police detained 261 suspects of seven nationalities (153 Chinese, 61 Vietnamese, 36 Thai and others) over an alleged telecom-fraud and online gambling operation in the Thatluang Lake SEZ; the outlet counted 550+ detentions in August.
record.attribution: Vientiane Capital Police, via Laotian Times

record.title: Flood watch as Mekong nears warning levels
record.detail: DMH reported the Mekong at 11.11 m at Vientiane Km4 (warning 11.50 m), 12.92 m at Thakhek (warning 13 m), 10.82 m at Pakse, and the Xe Don at Souvannakhili at 10.28 m, above its 10 m warning level.
record.attribution: Department of Meteorology and Hydrology, via KPL

record.title: Xe Lanong 1 dam to release water; Nam Theun 2 halts discharge
record.detail: Savannakhet authorities said Xe Lanong 1 hydropower dam would start releasing water from 11 Aug as inflows were forecast to rise from ~650 to up to 4,000 m3/s, and told nine downstream districts to warn residents; Nam Theun 2 Power Company said it suspended generation and releases into the Xe Bangfai from 7 Aug.
record.attribution: Savannakhet Provincial Administration and Nam Theun 2 Power Company, via The Star

record.title: Lao-Thai border checkpoints post sharp H1 revenue growth
record.detail: Lao Customs reported H1 2026 revenue of LAK 1.79 trillion at the 2nd Lao-Thai Friendship Bridge and LAK 996 billion at Vangtao (up 85%), with Lalai up 855% and 110,000+ travellers through the new 5th bridge, reflecting heavier cross-border trade.

record.title: 1.76 tonnes of suspected ivory seized in Pakkading
record.detail: Bolikhamxay authorities detained 11 foreign nationals and seized about 1,755.6 kg of items resembling elephant ivory and two carcasses resembling black panthers, and said they were tracing the wider network.
record.attribution: Bolikhamxay provincial authorities, via The Star

record.title: Floods affect more than 10,000 in Savannakhet
record.detail: Flooding hit at least 11 villages in Phin and Sepone districts, affecting more than 10,000 people, with three temporary shelters opened; the Mekong at Pakse reached 11.52 m on 19 Aug, above the 11 m alert level, and flash floods were reported in Sekong and Nan district of Luang Prabang.
record.attribution: Lao local authorities, via Khaosod English

record.title: Dengue cases reach 4,371 nationwide
record.detail: KPL reported 4,371 cumulative dengue cases as of 24 Aug with no deaths; Vientiane Capital had the most (706), followed by Sekong (530), Oudomxay and Vientiane Province (459 each) and Khammouane (424).

record.title: Public Security minister orders nationwide push after SIM-box raid
record.detail: After a 26 Aug raid in Lakhin and Houayhom villages, Sikhottabong district, seizing laptops, SIM boxes and transmission equipment (2 arrested), Minister of Public Security Lt Gen Vanthong Kongmany ordered intensified suppression of hidden cybercrime and online gambling nationwide.
record.attribution: Minister of Public Security Vanthong Kongmany, via KPL

record.title: Floods cut Route 13 North to Boten and leave 3,800+ Oudomxay homes without power
record.detail: Flooding and landslides on 28-29 August closed National Route 13 North from the Oudomxay border to Boten, hit 34 villages in Luang Namtha and 74 in Oudomxay, where at least 3,817 households lost power; repair crews were slowed by blocked roads.
record.agency: Provincial authorities / Department of Public Works and Transport

record.title: Laos tallies 6,200+ cybercrime arrests in eight months
record.detail: Laotian Times counted at least 6,200 cybercrime suspects arrested Jan-Aug 2026 from 25+ nationalities, including 139 at two Xaysettha buildings on 31 Aug and 47 in Paklay district, Xayaboury, with Chinese nationals the largest group in most raids.
record.attribution: Laotian Times compilation of Lao police reports

record.title: OFAC designates Xinbi Guarantee, listed with Laos location
record.detail: OFAC designated the Xinbi Guarantee online marketplace as a transnational criminal organization, listing Burma, Thailand and Laos as locations; Treasury said it processed the equivalent of over USD 24 billion serving scam and laundering networks.
record.attribution: US Treasury Office of Foreign Assets Control

record.title: Suspected rhino horn and ivory seized in Luang Prabang
record.detail: Luang Prabang's Natural Resources and Environment Inspection Division seized 28 kg of suspected rhinoceros horn, carved ivory, bile and wildlife-based medicines in Sanghalok village and detained a foreign man.
record.agency: Luang Prabang Natural Resources and Environment Inspection Division
record.attribution: Luang Prabang Provincial Natural Resources and Environment Inspection Division, via Laotian Times

record.title: 13 held in Vientiane raids; guns and meth found
record.detail: A Ministry of Public Security task force raided rentals in Chanthabouly and Hadxaifong districts, arresting 12 Chinese nationals and one Lao woman and seizing phones, computers, two handguns with ammunition and 1,494 suspected meth pills.
record.attribution: Ministry of Public Security task force, via KPL

record.title: 129 Thai nationals handed over after Vientiane and Champasak raids
record.detail: Following raids including 41 foreigners at Vientiane hotels on 16 Sep and 23 in Bachiang Chaleunsouk, Champasak on 18 Sep, 129 Thai nationals were handed to Thai authorities at the First Lao-Thai Friendship Bridge on 20 Sep.

record.title: Laos-Thailand seminar on laundering tied to scam centres
record.detail: Lao agencies, the Thai embassy and UNODC met in Laos on preventing laundering linked to scam centres, covering urgent asset freezes, mule accounts and crypto misuse; Laos aims to complete measures by January 2027.
record.attribution: Seminar participants incl. Lao authorities and UNODC, via The Nation

record.title: Navy intercepts trawlers with 600+ kg heroin/ice and firearms
record.detail: Navy intercepted a multi-day fishing trawler in the southern seas carrying over 600 kg of heroin and crystal meth plus T-56 and M-16 rifles and pistols; a second vessel that came to assist was also seized, 10 suspects arrested, vessels taken to Dikkowita.
record.attribution: Per Sri Lanka Navy, via Newsfirst; described as the largest haul of 2026 at that time

record.title: Health Promotion Bureau warns of leptospirosis
record.detail: Health Promotion Bureau said about 13,000 leptospirosis cases and nearly 300 deaths were recorded within a year.

record.title: 135 held in Chinese-run scam operation in Anuradhapura
record.detail: Immigration authorities raided an alleged Chinese-run online scam site, arresting 135 people incl. 126 Chinese nationals, mostly for tourist-visa violations; computers and phones seized. Officials called it the biggest such raid since Oct 2024.
record.attribution: Per Sri Lankan immigration officials via AFP

record.title: Government orders power-saving measures to avert grid collapse
record.detail: Government spokesman Nalinda Jayatissa said consumption must fall at least 25% as the Middle East war pushed up fuel costs; streetlights and billboards were switched off, state air-conditioning cut, and a four-day week and work-from-home reinstated.

record.title: Heat index 'Caution level' alert for 14 districts
record.detail: Department of Meteorology said the heat index could reach 'Caution level' on 26 March in Western, Sabaragamuwa, Southern and North-western provinces and Anuradhapura, Mannar, Vavuniya and Monaragala districts.
record.place: Western, Sabaragamuwa, Southern, North-western provinces + 4 districts
record.attribution: Advisory issued by the Department of Meteorology, via Newswire

record.title: Seven Rameswaram fishermen arrested near Neduntheevu
record.detail: Navy arrested 7 Rameswaram fishermen and seized two mechanised trawlers near Neduntheevu (Delft) islet, prompting protests in Thangachimadam, Tamil Nadu.

record.title: 152 foreigners arrested at Chilaw hotel scam hub
record.detail: Police and immigration raided a rented hotel in Chilaw, arresting 152 foreigners (133 Chinese, 13 Vietnamese, 6 others) and seizing 143 laptops, 120 desktops and 370 phones; two men were hurt trying to flee.
record.attribution: Per Sri Lanka Police via AFP

record.title: 12 Indian fishermen held off Jaffna
record.detail: Navy arrested 12 Tamil Nadu fishermen and seized a trawler near Jaffna for alleged poaching; report said over 100 Indian fishermen had been detained so far in 2026.

record.title: Nine Chinese arrivals from Kunming stopped with hundreds of devices
record.detail: Customs intercepted nine Chinese nationals arriving from Kunming carrying hundreds of electronic devices suspected for scam operations.

record.title: Over 25,000 dengue cases so far in 2026
record.detail: National Dengue Control Unit reported 25,082 cases and 12 deaths in 2026, highest in Colombo, Gampaha, Matara, Galle, Ratnapura and Kalutara.
